exposure: direct puncture embolization of the internal iliac artery with hemostatic gelatin sponge particles
Direct puncture embolization of the internal iliac artery with hemostatic gelatin sponge particles
outcome: Complications (fever, buttock pain, acute limb ischemia)
cohort: Women with pernicious placenta previa and placenta accreta who underwent cesarean delivery between September 1, 2013, and February 28, 2015, at a center in China
finding: Direct puncture embolization of the internal iliac artery during cesarean delivery was found to be a safe and effective method to control hemorrhage in women with pernicious placenta previa and placenta accreta.
